decision.question: Should the support lead change billing ticket coverage this quarter, and which change should be piloted first?

affected.who: Customers with billing questions and the two billing-trained agents
affected.process: Support ticket triage and first response

problem_statement: Billing tickets wait more than three times longer for a first reply than other tickets, while headcount cannot grow before 2027.

statements.text: Billing tickets had a median first response of 31 hours versus 9 hours for other tickets in October 2026.
Billing was 38 percent of the 1240 October tickets.
23.8 percent of billing tickets were reopened.
Billing first response is 3.4 times slower than other tickets.
Only 2 agents are trained on billing and both work weekday day shifts.
Billing questions arriving on Friday after 15:00 wait until Monday.
No new support headcount before 2027-01-01; the Q4 2026 tooling budget is 3000 USD.
Most billing questions are repetitive enough for reply macros.
Thin billing coverage outside weekday day shifts drives much of the billing delay.
Billing tickets queue behind the two trained agents because other agents cannot answer them.
Whether slow billing replies lower customer satisfaction is unknown.
statements.resolution: Add a one-question satisfaction prompt to closed billing tickets for four weeks.

statements.text: Whether billing delays contribute to cancellations is unknown.
statements.resolution: Ask finance for cancellation reasons tagged billing over the last two quarters.

alternatives.summary: Cross-train two more agents on billing with a reply macro library.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Uses training time now; reduces dependence on two people; macro quality is an assumption.

alternatives.summary: Add a Friday-afternoon and evening billing rota from existing agents.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Targets the arrival-time hypothesis directly; shifts existing workload and needs agent agreement.

alternatives.summary: Keep current coverage and only start measuring satisfaction.
alternatives.tradeoffs: No cost now; the delay continues while the satisfaction unknown is resolved.

success_measure.metric: Median first response for billing tickets

questions.text: Which agents could join a Friday-afternoon rota without overtime?

next_action.action: Split the October billing tickets by arrival time before choosing a pilot: if Friday-after-15:00 arrivals do not wait materially longer, prefer cross-training over a rota.

nodes.test: Compare median first response for billing tickets that arrive Monday-Thursday daytime with those arriving Friday after 15:00; if the gap is small, reject.
Measure how often non-billing agents pick up and then reassign billing tickets; if reassignment is rare, reject.

why_tree.stop_reason: Both branches reach a testable cause; deeper whys (why only two agents were trained) are not needed for the next decision.

partition.criterion: Where the delay arises: when tickets arrive (time coverage) versus who can answer them (skill coverage).
partition.overlaps: A Friday-evening ticket is affected by both: no trained agent works then.
partition.omitted: Tool latency and ticket tagging errors are not covered by the supplied evidence.
partition.interaction_assessment: The branches interact: adding trained agents only helps off-hours tickets if they also cover those hours, so the arrival-time split decides which lever to pilot first.

scqa.question: Which coverage change can bring billing first response near other tickets without new headcount?

provisional_answer.text: Pilot the lever the arrival-time split favors; candidate only until measured.

issue_map.overlaps: Off-hours tickets sit in both branches.

outcome.definition: Median hours from ticket creation to first agent reply, billing-tagged tickets.

leading_problems.text: Billing tickets arrive when no trained agent works
Only two agents can answer billing

edges.label: causal-hypothesis
edges.falsification: Arrival-time split shows no material wait difference.

edges.label: causal-hypothesis
edges.falsification: Reassignment of billing tickets by other agents is rare.

hypothesis.intervention: Friday-afternoon and evening billing rota from existing agents
hypothesis.rationale: Off-hours arrivals wait until Monday when no trained agent works.
hypothesis.measurement: Ticket export median first response, billing tag, before and after the pilot
hypothesis.counter_metric: Median first response for non-billing tickets must not rise above 12 hours
hypothesis.failure_rule: If billing median stays above 18 hours after 28 days, stop the rota and pilot cross-training.

one_page_prd.problem: Billing questions wait far longer for a first reply than other tickets.
one_page_prd.users: Customers with billing questions; support agents
one_page_prd.objective: Bring billing first response close to other tickets without new headcount.
scope: Off-hours billing rota pilot for 28 days
acceptance_tests: Billing median first response <= 12 hours over 28 days in the ticket export
Non-billing median first response stays <= 12 hours
risks: Seasonal billing volume changes confound the comparison
one_page_prd.next_decision: After 28 days: keep the rota, switch to cross-training, or combine.
